newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar crawls near lows vs yen by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar crawls near lows vs yen by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0637 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar crawled near the day's low versus the yen by late Tokyo afternoon trade on Monday after trimming its earlier gains on long liquidation and sales by Japanese exporters, dealers said.
The greenback was locked in tight ranges throughout the day, with bids by Japanese investors providing support around 114 yen and offers by exporters capping it near 115 yen.
The market lacked a convincing driving force to move out decisively from the New York ranges on Friday.
The greenback reached its peak of 114.70 yen on expectations of month-end commercial buying at Japan's local fixing, but the strength was brief, dealer said.
Dealers said that commercial buying demand was not as large as they had anticipated, which triggered some loss-cut sales from interbank dealers and speculators.
"Speculators quickly dumped their longs as the dollar's gains were limited at 114.70 yen. Exporters' sales also weighed on the dollar," a spot dealer at a Japanese city bank said.
The dollar/mark rate was dragged down by the greenback's fall against the yen after hitting a high of 1.7420 marks.
"It seems that there is selling interest when the dollar climbs above 1.74 marks," the dealer said. "The market's focus is zooming into the movements of European currencies."

On Friday in New York, the dollar hit a 10-day high against the mark after European officials continued to suggest that key European countries might fail to meet economic targets for monetary union. The dollar was at 114.58/68 yen and 1.7390/00 marks in late New York on Friday.

The Singapore dealers said they were watching the reaction to the rate cut by the Bank of Italy, which was announced on Friday when most markets had already closed. The bank cut its official discount rate to nearly a 22-year low of 6.25 percent.

"Its (Italy) rate cut would be good for its EMU entry but on the other hand, it means less returns," a dealer in Singapore said. "Mark/lira should then go up and if people keep buying mark and dollar/mark should go down."
The cross market was also dull. The mark fell slightly on the yen, with exporters' showing interest to sell marks above 66 yen and further, Tokyo dealers said.

The market was hungry for fresh market-moving incentives, and will be searching for clues from a series of events scheduled this week, including U.S. employment data for June on Thursday and the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday, dealers said.

"The Fed is highly unlikely to tighten at this week's FOMC, so the dollar is likely to be range-bound," a U.S. bank dealer in Tokyo said. "Operators are also not likely to build up large positions ahead of the long weekend in the U.S."
